DiskCache.swift:87-117: freshPayloadWithAge, hasFreshPayload and anyPayloadWithAge now hold three copies of the same stat -> mtime -> age block. Extract a private `payloadAge() -> TimeInterval?` so the TTL and maxStale rules are applied to a single age computation. A test pins the boundary today, but the copy-paste invites drift.

VendorViewModel.swift:166-175 (CORRECTNESS, not quality): the rate-limit cooldown is now stamped with the dispatch time, not the response time. A 429 that arrives after a long request therefore gets a cooldown shorter than rateLimitCooldown(forAttempt:). The comment admits this ('measured from dispatch, not arrival'), but it is worth confirming this is intended.

OpencodeScanner.swift:284-287: `.unavailable` groups caller configuration errors (an alias mapped to two groups, or an empty alias set) with SQLite read failures. CostEstimator therefore keeps stale rows forever when the configuration is wrong. Consider a separate case, or an assertion, for caller misuse.

dependabot.yml:26: Dependabot inserts ': ' after the prefix, so subjects read 'ci(deps) [skip release]: bump ...'. auto-tag still matches, because the marker can appear anywhere in the message. Check that the squash-merge head message keeps the PR title.

LOW docs sync: CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md never mention .github/dependabot.yml. The Releasing section should say that Dependabot github-actions PRs carry '[skip release]' by config, and the TOMLKit known-limitation note should say that Dependabot's swift ecosystem now watches it and a PR there is a prompt to re-evaluate, not an instruction to merge. Otherwise a maintainer who edits the prefix will not know the release rule depends on it.

LOW release hygiene: when a GitHub Actions bump changes a workflow's behavior (for example select-swift or the runner image), '[skip release]' means no validated tag reflects the new CI until the next code push. That is acceptable, but it is worth one line in the 'Where releases actually go wrong' table.
